correctness.rationale: Uniform Prufer words conditioned on exactly j distinct labels give the stated Stirling surjection mass formula. Size bias has normalization N/n. Real-rooted Bell polynomials entail Stirling row log concavity, then a strict decreasing t-ratio. Hence the comparison of consecutive j conditional size-biased multiplicities is monotone likelihood ratio including endpoint masses. Convex-payoff increments transfer the stochastic order to tagged degrees at invariant mean. Exact test of minors/hinges and full n<=8 word enumeration confirms finite cases but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The number of leaves is the primary degree-concentration statistic of uniform Cayley trees. All tagged degree means stay invariant, yet every strictly convex degree cost rises strictly at each adjacent feasible leaf count, a strong nontrivial concentration ordering not implied by the standard leaf-count enumeration. The size-biased likelihood-ratio law explains the mechanism and yields exact conditional moment/variance formulas and extreme cases. This is a structural finite-sample fact relevant to degree-energy and network hub concentration, not an arbitrary isolated number.
